correctness.rationale: The transfer matrix T=[[1,1],[1,0]] and occupancy projector D determine all finite-cycle moments with the exact trace normalization L_n. The covariance row is [r^d+r^{n-d}]/[5(1+r^n)]+r^n/[5(1+r^n)^2]; geometric DFT gives γ/4 and the precision symbol. Centered coordinate independence follows from the all-zero and n unit strings. Even n≥6 uses n^3(2/5)^n<1 for the zero-mode bound; odd n≥7 uses 4/n² trigonometric lower bound, with n=5 calculated separately. Expanding the exact quotient gives 5√5 n s^n (even) and 5π²/n² (odd). Independent enumeration n=5..12 reproduced all means, covariances, Fourier eigenvalues, positivity and mode extrema. This is an all-n analytic argument, not extrapolation from enumeration.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks confirm only the sampled sizes and parameter instances; the theorem must rest on the inspected all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The first Walsh band on cyclic hard-core configurations is a canonical finite sampling problem. The complete positive spectrum and inverse covariance give condition and precision operators for all n, while the parity-different sharp convergence is a nontrivial finite-size phenomenon. The exact all-size result is useful independently of any higher-band generalization.
residual_risks: The assessed value is limited to the precise natural family and invariant in the final claim, not any unstated generalization.
